title: Cap. I opening: Solomon to the Church — human affairs empty; nothing new under the sun
english: These are the words of Solomon, son of David the king and prophet, spoken to the whole Church of God — a king most honored among all people, and a prophet most wise.

How empty and unprofitable are the affairs of human beings, and all the eager pursuits that are merely human! For no one can name any lasting benefit attached to the things people crawl after on the earth, straining with body and soul to finish them — overcome by what is temporary, and unwilling to look up, even a little, above the stars with the noble eye of the soul.

And the life of human beings is worn away day by day, through the circuits of hours and years and the bounded courses of the sun: some arriving, others departing. The matter is like the passage of winter torrents falling into the measureless deep of the sea with much turmoil.

But the things God has made for the sake of human beings remain the same — for example, being born from the earth and departing into the earth; the earth itself standing firm; the sun going all around it and running back to the same bound; and likewise the winds, and the rivers that pour so great a volume into the sea, and the winds that beat upon it, without forcing the sea beyond its measures, and without themselves breaking their appointed order.

And so those things that contribute to this life of ours have been fixed. But the words and deeds that humans devise have no measure. There is a great throng of words, yet no benefit from that wandering babble. The human tribe is insatiable both for speaking and for hearing another speak — and still longs to look with idle eyes at each thing that happens to fall before it.

What could come later that has not already been finished, or that humans might still do? What is new that has not yet come into experience, and that is even worth remembering? For my part I think there is nothing; whatever someone may call recent or new, on reflection he will find it was not unknown to those of old. Just as former things have been hidden by forgetfulness, so also the present will be dimmed for those who come after, by time.

And I am not improvising these things now as I assemble the Church; rather, having been entrusted with the kingdom of the Hebrews in Jerusalem, I have considered all things carefully enough. (cf. Ecclesiastes 1:1-11)
